In [[number theory]], '''Waring's prime number conjecture''' is a [[conjecture]] related to [[Vinogradov's theorem]], named after the English mathematician [[Edward Waring]]. It states that every [[odd number]] exceeding 3 is either a [[prime number]] or the sum of three prime numbers. It follows from the [[generalized Riemann hypothesis]],<ref>{{cite journal |author-link1=Jean-Marc Deshouillers |first1=J.-M. |last1=Deshouillers |first2=G. |last2=Effinger |first3=H. |last3=te Riele |first4=D. |last4=Zinoviev |title=A complete Vinogradov 3-primes theorem under the Riemann Hypothesis |journal=Electr. Res. Ann. of AMS |volume=3 |year=1997 |pages=99–104 }}</ref> and ([[Triviality (mathematics)|trivially]]) from [[Goldbach's weak conjecture]].
